summary: Turns the search page into a client component that reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and renders them in a list. It also removes the search form.

findings.title: URL query rendered as raw HTML
findings.problem: The heading passes the q URL parameter into dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitizing it. React therefore inserts attacker-controlled markup into the page.
findings.consequence: An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect refetches on every render
findings.problem: The useEffect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each fetch calls setResults with a new array, which triggers another render and another fetch.
findings.consequence: The page sends search requests to the catalog API in an endless loop while it stays open. This wastes client and server resources.
findings.fix: Give the effect a dependency array containing query.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.problem: SearchPage returns early when q is missing, before it calls useState and useEffect. The number of hooks therefore changes when q goes from empty to set.
findings.consequence: React throws a hook order error when the user navigates between /search and /search?q=x. The page then crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Skip the fetch inside the effect when query is empty.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement
findings.problem: The change deletes the only search form in the repository. The page now says to type a search term but offers no input.
findings.consequence: Users have no way to enter a query. They can only search by editing the URL by hand.
findings.fix: Keep the form with the q input on the page, and render the results below it.

findings.title: Search failure is never handled
findings.problem: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok, but the promise chain has no catch handler. The rejection goes unhandled.
findings.consequence: Users see stale or empty results with no error message when the API fails. The browser only logs an unhandled rejection.
findings.fix: Add a catch handler that stores an error state and renders a message.

findings.title: List items have no key
findings.problem: The results list renders each li without a key. Product has a stable id field that could serve as the key.
findings.consequence: React cannot match items between renders when the results change. It logs a warning and may reuse the wrong elements.

findings.title: New search behaviour has no test
findings.problem: SearchPage now fetches products and renders results, but no test file covers this. The change adds no tests either.
findings.consequence: Regressions in fetching, rendering or the empty query path can ship without anyone noticing.
findings.fix: Add a component test for the empty query path, the results path and the API failure path.
